The Discussion on Mind as Object:
Is the knowledge in the penetration of others' minds (cetopariya-ñāṇa) necessarily having only mind as its object and not another object? Yes.
Is it not the case that there is someone who understands a mind with lust as "a mind with lust"? Yes.
If indeed there is someone who understands a mind with lust as "a mind with lust," then surely, alas, you should not say [that such understanding does not exist].
“Knowledge of the penetration of minds has only mind as its object, not another object.
Is it not the case that there is someone who [knows] a mind free from lust … pe … a mind possessed by hatred …?
A mind free from hatred… a deluded mind… a mind free from delusion…
A contracted mind...
a distracted mind...
an exalted mind...
a mind that is not sublime … a surpassable mind … an unsurpassable mind …
A concentrated mind … an unconcentrated mind … a liberated mind … [and so on] …
"One understands an unliberated mind as 'an unliberated mind'?
"Yes.
"If there is someone who understands an unliberated mind as 'an unliberated mind,' then indeed, you should not say—"
“Knowledge of the penetration of minds has mind as its object alone,
not another object. Should knowledge that has contact as its object be called “knowledge of the penetration of minds”?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If it must be said that knowledge regarding the object of contact is ‘knowledge of penetration of minds,’ then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘Knowledge of penetration of minds has mind alone as its object and nothing else as its object.’”
Knowledge regarding the object of feeling … pe … knowledge regarding the object of perception … knowledge regarding the object of volition …
Knowledge regarding the object of mind … knowledge regarding the object of faith … knowledge regarding the object of energy …
Knowledge with existence as its object...
knowledge with concentration as its object...
knowledge with wisdom as its object...
Knowledge with lust as its object...
knowledge with hatred as its object... knowledge with delusion as its object... and so forth.
Should it be said that knowledge regarding the object of non-fear (anottappa) is "knowledge of penetration of minds"?
Yes, it should.

If knowledge regarding the object of non-shame is to be called "knowledge of penetration of minds," then indeed it should not be said that "knowledge of penetration of minds has mind alone as its object and no other object.
Knowledge regarding the object of contact should not be so called.

It should not be said thus … [and so on] … knowledge regarding the object of feeling … [and so on] … knowledge regarding the object of perception … [and so on].
Is knowledge with fearlessness as its object not to be called "knowledge of penetration of minds"? Yes.
Is it to be said that “knowledge regarding the discourse on moral dread” [is knowledge]?
One should not say so … [as before] … It should not be said.
“Is the knowledge of the penetration of minds (cetopariya-ñāṇa) an object of mind alone and not an object of anything else?”—
Yes. But is it not indeed the knowledge of the penetration of minds?
“Yes.
“If there is knowledge of the penetration of minds, then indeed it must be said:
‘Knowledge of the penetration of minds has mind alone as its object, and not anything else as its object.’”
The Discussion on Mental Objects is finished.
